summary:
I opened every source file and checked each number, date, name and tag in the outline. No numeric error was found. Every figure on the 13 main slides and the 14 appendix slides matches the tables, and I recomputed the derived values (the steel balance, the CBAM worked example, shares, phase-in table, minute totals) from the displayed inputs. Defects are confined to wording, tags and internal consistency, plus the facts the sources say must be refreshed before November.

Conventions used below. Slide numbers 1-13 are main slides. Slides 101-114 are appendix A1-A14. Slide 0 means the approach, conflict log, dependencies or risks. Evidence abbreviations: RB = sources/text/inter-trade-present-2-revised-research-brief.txt (the update tab, line numbers from that file). BASE = sources/text/inter-trade-present-base.txt (line numbers from that file; its lines 257-491 duplicate RB). CHAT = sources/line-chat/line-inter-trade-chat.txt. BRIEF = notes/project-brief.md. DRAFT = Member B's slide draft. NOTES3 = the Thai five-topic notes. I also opened sources/images/base-doc-fig-01.png and -02.png.

Findings that need action:
1. Slide 5, BEFORE strip: the 2024 electricity value (16.77 ct/kWh) sits under BEFORE, but reporting began 1 Oct 2023, so 2024 belongs to DURING. The series is also the no-concession one (BASE 752); the same notes give 10.47 ct/kWh for eligible energy-intensive firms in 2024 (BASE 763). Label it "companies without reductions" and move 2024.
2. Slide 9: the visual says BMW is "appendix only", but BMW is Row 3's buyer on the same slide and in dropped_from_main. Delete BMW from that sentence.
3. Section 6(b), the dependencies and the risks use "G2" and "G4" for Member D's graph numbers, while the tag legend defines [G2] as the Export Policy lecture and [G4] as the EC ETS page. Write "Fig. 2" and "Fig. 4" there.
4. A7 explains the post-2005 import rise as "mostly free allocation and strong demand". The sources support free allocation only; "strong demand" is not in any source.
5. Slide 10, Tax row: "ETS and CBAM receipts are not German tax or G" is stronger than the sources, which say "not automatically" (BASE 93, 95; RB 40).
6. Conflict (e): the Thai notes' "no complete 1999-2025 series" is superseded only for the Chapter 72 aggregate. Per-product series (7204, 7207, 7208, 7304, 7306, 26011200) still exist only for 2019-25 (7208) or 2025.
7. Tag mismatches: slide 3 cites U3 for the certificate-price statement (the source tags it U4/U5); slide 12 cites U12/U20 for the four conditions (the list comes from untagged BASE 209).
8. Wording: "power-led" (slides 2 and 12) is stronger than "power-sector developments were an important driver"; "small" scenario GDP effects (slide 12) is stronger than "smaller and sensitive to model assumptions".
9. Slide 4: Dataset B ends in 2024, so "all data end in 2025" should read "end by 2025".

Needs-refresh items (true at the workbook date; the sources say to refresh before November): Q4 2026 certificate price (only Q1-Q3 published); Stegra status; downstream CBAM extension status (U32); the CBAM/ETS legal timeline and the steel quota text; 2026 trade data; provisional 2023-25 GVA, including the 19.4% headline; Dataset F first-estimate vintage; the August and September 2026 Commission items (S11, S23); the untagged BaseNotes electricity series.

I could not verify from the repository the references to "Draft A/B/C" in the approach paragraph. They are process notes, not source claims.
